transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Priya (AstraHealth), Mark (Astra infra), Jamal (Astra PM)
Recorded: yes (auto)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Reviewed Dedicated pool sizing for AstraHealth POC; discussed autoscale policies, burst capacity, and warm pool strategies.
- Agreed to run a 2-hour synthetic peak to validate throughput and KV cache behavior.
- Action items assigned for pricing, tests, and traffic percentile data.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got most of the key folks, um, quick run-through of agenda, dedicated capacity sizing insights from last week's benchmark and then we want to align on autoscale policies and the planned burst window test.
[00:14] Priya: hey all, thanks, we have about 45 minutes, i'll try to keep updates short, we did a quick internal look at yesterday's stress run — saw a few things around cache misses on long-context threads.
[00:26] Devon: cool, uh quick note — i pushed a kernel-level tweak in the sandbox, the seq-len distribution was slightly off so the GPU utilization was not ideal; we adjusted batch scheduling and that raised throughput ~8% in the non-quant run.
[00:41] Mark: yep saw that in the trace, devon, thanks. also, just to flag, our infra team is very sensitive to burst billing — we need predictability. so any recommended burst policy has to be quantifiable in cost terms.
[00:55] Sofia: totally, and that's why we'll cover the pricing delta for the burst add-on. quick poll — are we still targeting 1M tokens/hour steady-state with 1.5x peaks? Jamal?
[01:06] Jamal: that's still the internal target — product needs to be responsive during campaign windows and some mornings spike to 1.3–1.5x baseline for 20–45 minutes.
[01:19] Priya: and the 99th perc latency target from our side is under 300ms for short queries (<=512 tokens) — for long-form generation we accept higher but want consistent tail.

[00:62] Devon: (laughter) quick math — so for baseline 1M tokens/hr we're looking at sustained GPU concurrency, depends on batch size and cache hit rates. in our last run, with prefix caching enabled, effective tokens/second jumped by about 20% at 95th pct traffic.
[02:20] Sofia: can you unpack that a bit devon — what's the delta with warm vs cold kv cache?
[02:30] Devon: yeah, warm kv cache means prefix tokens (e.g., system prompts, shared context) are reused and we avoid recomputing. on a dedicated pool we can keep more KV in memory because there are pinned gpus for the tenant — that reduces per-token compute and latency. cold starts where the cache isn't populated cause 30–50% higher latency for that request.
[02:47] Priya: that's consistent with what we saw — the first few sessions after idle had spikes. what's your suggestion for warm pool sizing?
[02:55] Devon: practically, keep a warm pool of N workers equal to expected burst concurrency; for AstraHealth, given your 1.5x peaks, i'd recommend baseline pool = 6 workers and burst pre-warm up to 10 for the short spikes. that avoids cold starts.
[03:10] Mark: what is a worker in this context — a single GPU instance? we run on G5x-ish, is that one worker per GPU?
[03:18] Devon: yes, worker ~ 1 GPU process (could be multi-instance per node depending on instance sizing). we size by tokens/sec per GPU. in your env, a single A100 or G5 can handle about X tokens/sec depending on quantization and seq len — i'll include the calibrated numbers in the follow-up sheet.
[03:36] Jamal: cost tradeoffs — could we do more aggressive batching during baseline to shrink worker count?
[03:42] Devon: batching helps but increases latency. there's a sweet spot; for chat-latency workloads batching beyond 60ms queuing hurts UX. we can do dynamic batching: allow higher batch sizes in non-peak windows.

[04:00] Priya: on autoscale policy specifics — cooldown, ramp, and min/max pools — we have some internal guardrails. what does redwood recommend?
[04:09] Sofia: we've been recommending a conservative cooldown (60–120s) for rapid middleware bursts, with a ramp-up limit of say +2 workers per minute to prevent noisy scaling. but for short campaign spikes it's better to pre-warm.
[04:23] Mark: so pre-warm + limited autoscale — ok. what about burst billing thresholds, like when we start being charged for burst capacity?
[04:31] Sofia: burst is invoiced when the cluster uses capacity above the reserved pool; we can cap the total burst budget at a dollar amount per day for the pilot to control spend. i'll attach the pricing calc.
[04:42] Jamal: please do. also, there's the fallback model path — if Dedicated is saturated, can requests fall back to hosted endpoints?
[04:50] Devon: yes, smart routing allows fallback to compatible hosted model variants. note there's a potential cold-warm mismatch and we generally recommend the fallback only for short durations because of context / KMS differences.
[05:02] Priya: can the fallback preserve our PII/data controls? we need to avoid cross-tenant leakage.
[05:10] Sofia: hosted fallback will still honor data residency for the tenant if configured, but for strict regulatory scenarios we can disable fallback entirely. we'll document the tradeoff.

[05:30] Speaker 1 (auto): -- background noise --
[05:34] Devon: quick note on the KV eviction policy, AstraHealth's longer average context -> you might see evictions if the working set exceeds per-GPU KV memory. we can change atlas eviction thresholds or move to higher memory GPU.
[05:47] Mark: what's the impact in perf if we bump to higher memory nodes? is it linear?
[05:51] Devon: not linear — bigger KV means fewer evictions and better tail latency, but compute per token roughly same. so adoption is mostly tail and reduced recompute costs.

[06:05] Priya: regarding the synthetic test, what will you simulate? long-running threads plus chat — we need to emulate our morning campaign and a mid-day steady load.
[06:14] Devon: test plan: 2-hour window with a ramp from baseline to 1.5x at minute 30, hold 25–45 minutes, then ramp down. script also includes variance in seq lengths: 60% short (<256 tokens), 25% medium, 15% long. also simulate new sessions to stress kv cold starts.
[06:36] Jamal: will that include a canary traffic route to test fallback?
[06:40] Devon: yes — we'll reserve ~5% of traffic to route to hosted fallback for observability.

[07:00] Sofia: ok let's talk numbers — Priya, can you confirm your 95/99 percentile sequence length and QPS during peak?
[07:08] Priya: 95th seq len ~420 tokens, 99th ~980 tokens in the longer flows. qps during baseline ~45 requests/sec, peak reaches ~62 req/sec.
[07:20] Devon: great, that helps. with those distributions we estimate each GPU at your planned quantization profile does ~22–28 req/sec avg for mixed seq lengths, so baseline fleet of 6 GPUs covers baseline with headroom; burst up to 10 GPUs to meet spikes.
[07:36] Mark: can we do autoscale min=4 max=12 so we have headroom for unexpected events?
[07:42] Sofia: yes that's a reasonable range for pilot. we'll tune cooldown to 90s and ramp to +3 workers/minute unless we see oscillation.

[08:00] Priya: how will model versions be rolled in Dedicated? we need pinning for the pilot.
[08:07] Devon: you can pin by model-version at route level; we support canaries and gradual rollouts. for the test, pin to the exact model sha to avoid surprise regressions.
[08:16] Jamal: okay makes sense. any concern about the quantized variant vs full fp for quality? we noted small drop in rare hallucination tests.
[08:25] Devon: quantization tradeoffs exist; part of redwood optimize recommendations we'll share a small eval matrix: quantized variant + calibration prompts to measure delta. if reliability is critical, keep dedicated un-quantized for a subset of routes.

[09:00] Speaker 2 (auto): background typing
[09:04] Priya: sec question — logs and audit: do we get per-token breakdown and token-level cost? our finance wants a pretty granular chargeback.
[09:12] Sofia: yes, console provides token-level cost + per-route telemetry. for dedicated you can also get per-worker cost traces. we'll share a sample billing extract.
[09:22] Mark: what about retention of request logs? we need 90-days for debugging.
[09:27] Devon: retention configurable; default is 30 days in the pilot but we can extend to 90 with retention add-on. note this increases storage costs.

[10:00] Priya: any ops recommendations to reduce burst costs? besides pre-warm?
[10:06] Devon: yes — prefix caching, aggressive KV reuse, sharding long conversations to a subset of workers to maintain high locality, and trimming redundant system prompts server-side. also consider short TTL cache for seldom-used contexts.
[10:22] Jamal: what about using a cheaper quantized fallback during non-critical paths?
[10:26] Devon: totally viable — route non-critical generative tasks to quantized instances with larger batch windows.

[11:00] Sofia: quick pause — i'm going to share the pricing addon link in chat (Sofia shares: https://redwood.example/pilot-pricing/astrah-pilot-v2) — note the burst calculator tab.
[11:18] Mark: got it. opening now.
[11:24] Priya: seeing the estimated daily cap chart, can you walk through the assumptions for the burst cost calc?
[11:31] Sofia: assumptions: 1) baseline is reserved monthly commit, 2) burst rate billed at per-GPU minute rate, 3) pre-warm minutes counted as billed if the GPUs are reserved for you even if idle. we show two scenarios: pre-warm + short burst vs reactive autoscale.
[11:48] Mark: so pre-warm incurs cost even if not used — is there a partial minute granularity?
[11:52] Sofia: minute granularity yes, billing rounds to the minute; we can simulate sample days.

[12:20] Devon: technical note: if you plan to keep a pre-warmed pool for 45 minutes daily during campaigns, we recommend reserving a small burst quota to avoid overpaying reactive autoscale. it depends on your campaign predictability.
[12:34] Priya: our campaigns are predictable to the hour but not exact minute, so pre-warm for 15 mins before expected start then ramp may be ideal.
[12:41] Jamal: yes that's our preference.

[12:55] Sofia: ok — next, the synthetic stress window details and measurement plan. Devon will run test and we'll watch: latency percentiles, KV hit ratio, GPU utilization, mem pressure, scaling events, and fallback routing hits.
[13:10] Devon: i'll push a test job to the pilot namespace; i'll also stream a Grafana link and a Flamegraph snapshot. expect initial results by EOD 2025-11-07.
[13:21] Mark: what about secrets / KMS — the hosted fallback uses different KMS keys correct?
[13:26] Sofia: yes, if you use private deployment keys we can map keys; hosted fallback will use redwood-managed keys unless you bring-your-own. we'll include KMS mappings in the security packet.

[14:00] Priya: any other risk items? off the top — KV eviction and noisy neighbor if we overcommit nodes.
[14:08] Devon: true — Dedicated is isolated but under certain deployment topologies (shared hosts) you might still see contention; we recommend pinned nodes for the pilot (we can set node affinity to avoid collocation).
[14:21] Mark: pinned nodes sounds good — add to action items.
[14:26] Sofia: added.

[15:00] Jamal: timeline check — we want to conclude pilot validation in two weeks. is that feasible?
[15:06] Sofia: yes if tests run next week and we do one more tuning iteration we can decide on commit by end of week 2.
[15:14] Priya: fine.

[15:30] Devon: small gotcha — the model variant you're using has an updated tokenizer change in the newer release; if you plan to upgrade mid-pilot the token accounting changes; we advise you freeze model version during capacity tests.
[15:45] Priya: noted, we'll freeze.

[16:00] Sofia: all right let's recap — recap and next steps: run 2-hour synthetic peak (Devon+Mark), Sofia sends pricing & security docs, Mark to provide traffic percentiles and confirm pinned node requirement, schedule capacity validation Wed 10-12 PT. did i miss anything?
[16:20] Mark: no that's it.
[16:25] Priya: one ask — can you also surface a sample billing export for a hypothetical 7-day campaign? helps finance.
[16:32] Sofia: yes will do.

[17:00] Speaker 1 (auto): meeting ended

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker labels may be approximate. some jargon like "KV" and "prefix cache" were auto-corrected in places.
